rs1142345.explanation: In a cohort of 149 Chinese AIH/AIH–PBC variant patients genotyped for TPMT rs1142345, the study reported no significant association with AZA-induced leukopenia or maintenance dose; the risk-allele frequency was low (~1.7%), which may have limited power.

summary.summary:
## Background
Azathioprine (AZA) is commonly used for autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) and AIH–primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) overlap, but leukopenia is a serious adverse effect. In East Asian populations, TPMT variants explain little of this risk. This single-center retrospective study of 149 Chinese patients evaluated whether NUDT15 rs116855232 (R139C) and TPMT*3C rs1142345 variants predict AZA-induced leukopenia and influence dosing.

## Key Findings
- NUDT15 rs116855232 (C>T, R139C) strongly predicted leukopenia. Carriage of the T allele was associated with markedly higher risk (OR 20.41; 95% CI 7.84–53.13; P < 0.00001), with sensitivity 91.7% and specificity 89.1% for leukopenia. Leukopenia occurred in 37.5% of CT heterozygotes (9/24) and 100% of TT homozygotes (2/2) versus 0.8% of CC (1/123), typically within 60 days of starting/increasing AZA.
- NUDT15 variation affected thiopurine metabolism and tolerated dose: CT carriers had higher 6-thioguanine nucleotide (6-TGN) levels (median 276.6 vs 145.3 pmol/8×10^8 RBC; P = 0.002) and required lower AZA maintenance doses (median 0.96 vs 1.23 mg/kg/day; P = 0.028). The AZA dose-to–6-TGN ratio was lower in CT (P = 0.013). Overall, 6-TGN concentration did not distinguish those with vs without leukopenia (P = 0.149).
- TPMT*3C rs1142345 showed no significant association with leukopenia or dosing in this cohort; the risk allele was rare.
- In a subgroup with pre-existing leukopenia (n = 13), WBC counts did not worsen on AZA; most were NUDT15 wild-type and maintained typical doses (~1.13 mg/kg/day).

## Clinical Implications
- Preemptive NUDT15 genotyping should be considered alongside TPMT before initiating AZA in AIH, especially in East Asian patients. T-allele carriers (CT/TT) are at high risk for early leukopenia and need dose adjustments and close monitoring in the first 8 weeks.
- For NUDT15 CT heterozygotes, starting/maintaining AZA at about 1 mg/kg/day appears effective and safer; TT homozygotes may require very low doses or alternative immunosuppression.
- Routine TPMT*3C testing alone is insufficient in East Asians; NUDT15 provides substantially greater predictive value.
- 6-TGN levels alone may not predict leukopenia; genotype-guided dosing, potentially supplemented by metabolite monitoring, can optimize safety. Patients with baseline leukopenia from cirrhosis/hypersplenism may still tolerate AZA if NUDT15 is wild-type.
